Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the latest MSA. Our GC flagged the damages exclusion as a blocker — specifically the one-way consequential exclusion in section 9.2. They view the current draft as unfairly one-sided (it excludes Acme's consequential losses but not Redwood's), and asked whether we can agree one of the following:

1) Make the consequential/special/incidental/punitive exclusion fully mutual; or
2) Keep it one-way but add a narrowly tailored carve-out for: (a) data corruption/loss caused by Redwood's negligence, and (b) breach of confidentiality leading to regulatory fines.

I've attached our annotated redline (Acme_MSA_Redline_v3.docx). Can you share Redwood's position and any examples of conservative compromise language that would move this forward? Our procurement team needs a path to sign this month.

Best,

Joel — thanks for the clear note and the redline. We appreciate Acme's candor. Short answer: Redwood prefers mutual exclusions for consequential-type damages where possible, but we also need to preserve the commercial cap and carve-outs that align to our core risk (data theft, SOC obligations, and intentional misconduct). A couple of negotiation options we can propose quickly:

Option A — Mutual exclusion, tailored carve-outs - Make the consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages exclusion mutual.
- Add specific carve-outs that are not subject to the exclusion: (i) claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) claims arising from a breach of obligations under section X (confidentiality/data protection) that result in regulatory fines; and (iii) amounts payable under indemnities for third-party IP infringement (already in the MSA).

Option B — One-way exclusion with limited Acme remedies - Keep one-way exclusion (Redwood only limits its exposure) but add a narrow, enumerated exception giving Acme recovery for: (i) verified data loss/corruption caused by Redwood's breach of its documented backup/retention commitments; (ii) direct regulatory fines resulting from Redwood's failure to follow agreed security controls.

I included Marissa and Markus here — Marissa, could you weigh in on the specific drafting we should propose? Markus, flag if this drifts outside legal tolerance for one-way positions.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik/Joel — quick legal note from our side. We prefer Option A (mutual exclusion + narrow carve-outs). Mutuality reduces commercial friction with enterprise buyers and is acceptable when the exclusions are clearly limited. Proposed drafting (high level):

"Neither party shall be liable to the other for incidental, consequential, special, exemplary, or punitive damages, except for (i) damages resulting from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) damages arising from a party's breach of its confidentiality or data protection obligations that result in regulatory fines or statutory penalties; and (iii) amounts payable under Section Y (IP indemnity)."

Two implementation notes:
- Define "gross negligence" and "willful misconduct" narrowly (examples and thresholds) to avoid unbounded liability.
- If Acme insists on a one-way exclusion, we will require the commercial cap to be recalibrated upward (e.g., 6 months' fees -> 12 months' fees) to compensate for asymmetry.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — the mutual text looks reasonable, but GC is worried that 'gross negligence' is easily pled and will swallow the exclusion. Two follow-up asks from our counsel:

1) Can the mutual carve-out require a showing of "willful, intentional misconduct" for regulatory fines (i.e., higher threshold than simple gross negligence)?
2) If Redwood will not accept a one-way exclusion, we need a limited transition: a 12-month mutual exclusion period for the first year, after which Acme can request renegotiation tied to observed reliability metrics (SLA breaches >3 incidents or security incidents).

We're trying to avoid reopening pricing with procurement, so any language that ties cap movement to objective metrics rather than subjective claims will help.

Joel

Joel — quick follow-up after internal sync. We can accept the higher threshold for regulatory-fines carve-out language: require "willful, intentional misconduct" for fines to be recoverable (i.e., not covered by exclusion). For the other exceptions (data corruption/loss, IP indemnity), the gross negligence threshold remains.

Regarding the transition/metrics proposal: Redwood is open to a performance-linked renegotiation trigger as long as the trigger is objective and capped. Proposed trigger language: "Acme may request re-opening of the damages exclusion terms if, during any consecutive 12-month period, (i) Redwood experiences three or more SLA violations classified as Severity 1 affecting Acme, or (ii) Redwood reports a security incident resulting in confirmed unauthorized data exfiltration affecting Acme. Such request will be limited to negotiation of liability cap and exclusion terms and will not automatically change pricing or caps absent mutual agreement."

If that sounds acceptable, we'll produce a redline that (a) makes the exclusion mutual, (b) adds the enumerated carve-outs, (c) raises the burden-of-proof for regulatory-fines carve-out to willful/intentional misconduct, and (d) includes the objective renegotiation trigger.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
